main_text.p: ” fefsione fua Principes reti- ” nuerunt. nunc, ut honores, ” ut omnis dignitatis gradus, ” fic huius fcientiæ fplendor ” deletus eft: idqueeo indigni- ” us, quòd eo tempore hoc ” contigit, cum is effet qui om- ” nes superiores, quibus hono- ” re par effet, fcientia facilè vi- ” ciffet. hæc autem opera gra- ” ta multis, &ad beneficijs ad- ” ftringendos homines accom- ” modata. Hęc Cicero: Craf- fus autem apud eundem li- bro de Oratore 1. in eandem fententiam, cum dixiffet Ro- mæ amplifsimum quemque &clarifsimum virum Iuris fcientiæ præeffe, multosque cum

page.notes: Quotation marks ” at the start of each line are printed text of the quoted passage and are kept. The running head is set in spaced small capitals and could not be read letter by letter. Hyphenated line-end words kept as printed. "uiciffet" and "uirum" were read as printed letters with u/v adjusted to vi-ciffet and virum. The word "cum" at the foot is a catchword. "1." after Oratore is a printed reference number.
